original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

existing_checks.scope: Packing-independent ceiling for the selected paid profile under the one-unpaid-coordinate coverage and halving guard.
existing_checks.remaining: A changed word or model requires new pricing; a local packing search must name uncovered scope.

actual_scope: Certify the endpoint of the optimal integer idle packing of the selected fixed local word as a function of the legal idle rank cap, with an independently written exact rational pricing chain, and price the pooling, residue and per-call variants at the cap.
scope_change_reason: The fixed-word fractional ceiling and the unrestricted integer optimum are already delivered by the reviewed complex-local-word-ceiling and idle-packing-stability packages. The open question those packages name is the physical owner/hosting restriction on idle children. This package takes the first and crudest of those restrictions, a hard cap on the idle rank, and prices the optimum under every cap instead of searching for a new packing.
bottleneck_link: The packing headroom quoted for the selected complex word is +0.869% in kappa. This package certifies which part of it is independent of the idle rank cap and which part needs ranks above the largest rank the selected word itself uses, so the open physical-hosting effort can be judged against its actual return.
stop_rule: Finish the cap table, the four independently certified reproductions and the refusal controls; stop without a physical-realizability, supplier or frontier claim.
evidence: README.md statement and tables; RESULT.json certified brackets for 21 rank caps in four packing variants; verify.py registered replay with nine controls; enclosures.py is an independent rational enclosure chain.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which idle ranks are legally hostable in the selected physical template, above all whether ranks 49 to 51 can host idle remainder at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The certified aggregate optimum gains +0.870% at cap 51 but only +0.396% at the attested cap 48. The majority of the headroom needs ranks above the largest one the selected word uses.
open_questions.first_step: Extract one selected owner-family residual instance and test whether a rank-49 to rank-51 idle child satisfies the stated owner, port and halving contracts.
open_questions.blocked_by: No source-bound characterization of legal idle groups and hosting resources is available in this checkout.

open_questions.question: Does the pooled aggregate optimum survive the per-call distribution of the selected invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Requiring each call to reach its own optimum loses about 0.086 percentage points at cap 51, and the selected idle histogram is not per-call uniform either.
open_questions.first_step: Bind one call's actual idle remainder to its recorded owner slots and check whether the record already pools across calls.
open_questions.blocked_by: The selected owner ledger in this checkout is an aggregate histogram, not a per-call assignment.
